title: Spread density of an open into every geometric fibre
statement: Let f:X→T be a finite type scheme morphism, η a generic point of T, and W an open subscheme of X. Suppose both X_η and W_η are geometrically irreducible. There is an open U containing η such that for every t in U and every field K with Spec K→Spec κ(t), the canonical inclusion W_t×κ(t)Spec K→X_t×κ(t)Spec K has dense range. Geometric irreducibility includes nonemptiness.

source.place: Tag 054X (Lemma 37.24.3), its use in Tag 0559, second proof; Tag 0383.

proof.text: The open W_η is nonempty in the irreducible X_η, so is dense. Its closed complement Z_η is nowhere dense. Reduce the base to an integral scheme without changing fibre spaces. Generic flat finite presentation, applied to X and the reduced complement Z, gives a common generic neighbourhood where both morphisms are flat and locally finitely presented.

If Z_t has interior in X_t, choose a generic point ξ of an irreducible component of X_t in Z_t. Flatness of Z gives a generalization ξ′ in Z_η. Stacks Lemma 37.22.10 equates the fibre dimensions of Z and X at these points, contradicting the nowhere dense generic complement. This is the proof of Tag 054X and yields a neighbourhood where W_t is dense in X_t.

A residue-field extension is faithfully flat and universally open (Tag 0383), hence its base-change projection is an open surjection. The inverse image of W_t is dense. The canonical double pullback map in the statement is its open inclusion, so has dense range.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_geometric_fibre_dense_of_open {X T : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (W : X.Opens) (η : T) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hgeom : GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η))
    (hWgeom : GeometricallyIrreducible ((W.ι ≫ f).fiberToSpecResidueField η)) :
    ∃ U : T.Opens, η ∈ U ∧
      ∀ (t : T), t ∈ U → ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K]
        (z : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Spec (T.residueField t)),
        DenseRange (pullback.map ((W.ι ≫ f).fiberToSpecResidueField t) z
          (f.fiberToSpecResidueField t) z
          (pullback.map (W.ι ≫ f) (T.fromSpecResidueField t) f
            (T.fromSpecResidueField t) W.ι (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp))
          (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (by simp [Scheme.Hom.fiberToSpecResidueField]) (by simp))
